title: Optimizing the Weather Research and Forecasting Model with OpenMP Offload and Codee
problem: The Weather Research and Forecasting model (WRF) currently uses only CPU parallelism via OpenMP and MPI, failing to leverage GPU resources available on modern supercomputers. The computationally expensive Fast Spectral Bin Microphysics scheme requires GPU acceleration to improve simulation performance.
motivation: GPU-accelerated weather forecasting reduces time-to-solution for critical weather prediction tasks on modern HPC systems.
method: The authors move computationally expensive parts of the FSBM (Fast Spectral Bin Microphysics) scheme—which simulates cloud droplets in weather models—from CPUs to NVIDIA GPUs on the Perlmutter supercomputer, using OpenMP device offloading directives (commands that tell code to run on the GPU instead of the CPU). They combine two complementary tools to guide the work: runtime profilers (which measure performance while code executes) and Codee (a static code inspection tool that analyzes code before it runs) to find bottlenecks and spots where the code can be reorganized for faster GPU execution.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining static code inspection (analyzing code before it runs) with runtime profiling to systematically identify and optimize the computationally expensive parts of weather simulations for GPU execution.
contributions: Ported FSBM microphysical scheme to NVIDIA GPUs using OpenMP device offloading
Demonstrated practical workflow combining runtime profilers and static analysis (Codee) for GPU optimization
Achieved 2.08x overall speedup on CONUS-12km thunderstorm test case
Validated GPU acceleration approach for production weather simulation codes
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the provided abstract.
